Customer journey

Every stage, every handoff, every owner.

Follow the journey from first contact to repeat relationship. Each stage shows its touchpoints, the accountable role, and the automations that support it.

  1. 01Discover and inquire2 automations
  2. 02Apply, verify and decide4 automations
  3. 03Use and service1 automation
  4. 04Pay and renew2 automations
  5. 05Claims, disputes and alerts3 automations
  6. 06Review and grow2 automations
01

Discover and inquire

Prospects compare loans, policies, advisers and apps on search, social media and aggregators, or arrive through DSAs, agents and referrals. Clear information that stays within the advertising rules, and a fast, honest first reply, decide who earns the application.

Touchpoints

  • Search and social ads
  • Loan and insurance aggregators
  • DSA, agent and POSP referrals
  • WhatsApp and website inquiries
  • Adviser posts and newsletters

Accountable owner

Marketing or sales head, with the compliance officer

Automations on this stage

Discover and inquire · 3–5 weeks

Inquiry desk with indicative eligibility

Capture loan inquiries from ads, aggregators, the website, WhatsApp and DSAs, ask only what indicative eligibility needs, check it against the lender's published criteria, and route likely applicants to the right owner. It guides; it never decides.

View the blueprint ↗Discover and inquire · 2–4 weeks

Compliance-approved content library and distribution

Draft educational posts, newsletters and WhatsApp updates from approved source material, route each one to the compliance officer, and let advisers and agents share only approved, versioned items that carry the required disclosures.

View the blueprint ↗
02

Apply, verify and decide

The customer applies, shares documents and completes KYC, the regulated entity verifies them, and qualified people make the credit, underwriting, suitability or merchant approval decision. Most drop-offs and delays happen here.

Touchpoints

  • Application and proposal forms
  • Document upload and DigiLocker fetch
  • Video KYC and CKYC checks
  • Risk-profiling questionnaire
  • Merchant due diligence
  • KFS, sanction letter and agreement

Accountable owner

Operations or onboarding head; credit, underwriting or compliance decides

Automations on this stage

Apply, verify and decide · 6–10 weeks

Application, KYC and status tracker

Generate the right checklist for each application or proposal, collect documents through a secure page or DigiLocker, track KYC steps, chase what is missing, and keep the customer updated until a person makes the decision.

View the blueprint ↗Apply, verify and decide · 3–5 weeks

Client onboarding and risk-profiling workflow

Take a new advisory client from the first call to a signed agreement, KYC confirmed with a KRA, and a risk profile the client has reviewed and consented to, with every record kept together for the retention period.

View the blueprint ↗Apply, verify and decide · 3–5 weeks

Onboarding drop-off recovery for apps

Detect where users stall in sign-up, such as KYC, bank linking or mandate setup, identify the likely reason, and send one helpful, consented nudge or route the user to support instead of sending blanket reminders.

View the blueprint ↗Apply, verify and decide · 6–9 weeks

Merchant onboarding and due diligence queue

Collect merchant documents, run checks on PAN, GSTIN, bank account and website, assign a risk tier, and give onboarding officers one queue, so no merchant goes live before due diligence is complete and approved.

View the blueprint ↗
03

Use and service

After disbursal, issuance or onboarding, customers need statements, certificates, changes and answers. Consistent answers from approved documents, and fast routing of account-specific requests, prevent complaints.

Touchpoints

  • Statement and certificate requests
  • Policy, loan and investment queries
  • Nominee and address changes
  • Foreclosure letters and NOCs

Accountable owner

Customer service head

Automations on this stage

Use and service · 5–8 weeks

Servicing assistant grounded in approved documents

Answer policy, loan and investment servicing questions on WhatsApp and the website only from approved documents, with the source shown, and hand account requests, complaints and anything uncertain to a person with the context attached.

View the blueprint ↗
04

Pay and renew

EMIs and premiums fall due, mandates bounce and policies approach expiry. Timely reminders on the right channel keep accounts current, and overdue follow-up must respect RBI conduct rules and each channel's policy.

Touchpoints

  • Pre-due EMI reminders
  • NACH and UPI AutoPay mandate results
  • Insurer renewal notices
  • Payment links
  • Collections calls within permitted hours

Accountable owner

Collections head or renewals manager

Automations on this stage

Pay and renew · 4–6 weeks

EMI reminders and respectful collections workflow

Remind borrowers before each EMI, flag mandate bounces the same day, and run overdue follow-up through approved channels within RBI's conduct rules, with hardship cases routed to a trained officer.

View the blueprint ↗Pay and renew · 3–5 weeks

Renewal reminders for motor, health and life policies

Pull upcoming renewals from the broker system or insurer data, remind customers well before expiry with the insurer's quoted premium, explain what lapsing means for their cover, and route any change of cover to a licensed person.

View the blueprint ↗
05

Claims, disputes and alerts

When something goes wrong, such as a claim, a chargeback, a failed transaction or a suspicious payment, the customer needs quick acknowledgment and updates, and the person who decides needs a complete case file.

Touchpoints

  • Claim intimation and documents
  • Chargebacks and UPI disputes
  • Fraud alerts and customer verification
  • Complaints and ombudsman escalation routes

Accountable owner

Claims, disputes or risk operations head

Automations on this stage

Claims, disputes and alerts · 4–6 weeks

Claim intimation, checklists and status updates

Help policyholders intimate claims quickly, collect the right documents for each claim type, follow the claim with the insurer or TPA, and explain every status and query in plain language until settlement.

View the blueprint ↗Claims, disputes and alerts · 6–9 weeks

Dispute and chargeback operations queue

Bring card chargebacks, UPI disputes and failed-transaction complaints into one queue with deadlines, gather evidence automatically from ledgers and merchants, and give analysts a drafted response to review before anything is submitted.

View the blueprint ↗Claims, disputes and alerts · 6–10 weeks

Fraud alert triage for analysts

Enrich every fraud or risk alert with customer, device and transaction context, summarize the evidence, prioritize the queue by severity and time sensitivity, and record each analyst decision to improve the rules.

View the blueprint ↗
06

Review and grow

Good customers come back for a top-up, a renewal, a review or a new goal. Reviews and offers work when they follow the customer's needs and recorded consent, and when credit or suitability is decided by a person.

Touchpoints

  • Portfolio and goal reviews
  • SIP continuity check-ins
  • Top-up and renewal offers approved by credit
  • Gold loan renewals at maturity

Accountable owner

Relationship manager or adviser

Automations on this stage

Review and grow · 4–6 weeks

Portfolio reviews with SIP and goal check-ins

Schedule reviews from each client agreement, prepare a review pack from RTA and back-office data, flag missed SIPs and approaching goal dates, and remind clients on time, while the adviser makes every recommendation.

View the blueprint ↗Review and grow · 3–5 weeks

Top-up and renewal journeys approved by credit

Find borrowers who meet the lender's policy for a top-up or renewal review, get the credit team's approval for the list and offer terms, and reach consented customers with a fresh, fully disclosed application.

View the blueprint ↗

Where people stay in control

Human checkpoints across the journey.

Automation handles the predictable steps. These are the decisions that stay with an accountable person.

AutomationStageHuman checkpoint
Inquiry desk with indicative eligibilityDiscover and inquireIndicative results never promise approval, a rate or a limit. Credit assessment, bureau checks and the decision stay with the lender's credit team after a full application, and sales staff take over whenever the prospect asks for a person or the case is unusual.
Compliance-approved content library and distributionDiscover and inquireNothing is published or shared without the named compliance approver's sign-off and any approval the insurer or BASL must give. The workflow does not create return or performance claims, recommend specific securities or plans, or engage unregistered influencers.
Application, KYC and status trackerApply, verify and decideOperations officers verify documents and resolve KYC exceptions. Credit officers, underwriters or the insurer decide every application and record the reasons; the tracker never approves, declines, prices or sets limits.
Client onboarding and risk-profiling workflowApply, verify and decideThe SEBI-registered adviser finalizes every risk profile and suitability judgment and gives all advice. The questionnaire scores and flags; it never assigns a final profile or recommends products. For distributors, the workflow covers onboarding and service, not advice.
Onboarding drop-off recovery for appsApply, verify and decideOnboarding operations and compliance handle every KYC exception and decide edge cases. Product owners approve every message and frequency cap, and nudges never promise credit, limits or rewards outside approved terms.
Merchant onboarding and due diligence queueApply, verify and decideOnboarding officers approve or reject every merchant, and risk or compliance approves higher-risk tiers. Automated checks inform the decision; they never activate a merchant on their own.
Servicing assistant grounded in approved documentsUse and serviceService staff own every account change, complaint and exception, and the grievance redressal officer owns escalations. The assistant gives no advice on products, cover, claim outcomes or investments.
EMI reminders and respectful collections workflowPay and renewCollections officers decide settlements, restructuring, waivers, agent assignment and any legal step. The workflow never threatens, never contacts relatives or references, and never sends legal notices on its own.
Renewal reminders for motor, health and life policiesPay and renewA licensed agent or the broker's qualified staff handles every change of cover, insurer switch, portability request and disclosure question. The workflow reminds and informs; it does not recommend cover.
Claim intimation, checklists and status updatesClaims, disputes and alertsThe insurer or TPA decides every claim, and surveyors assess losses where required. The broker's claims executive verifies every submission and handles death claims personally; the workflow never predicts or promises an outcome.
Dispute and chargeback operations queueClaims, disputes and alertsDispute analysts decide every acceptance, representment and refund, and finance approves write-offs. Nothing is submitted to a network or bank without an analyst's approval.
Fraud alert triage for analystsClaims, disputes and alertsFraud analysts decide every hold, block, release and escalation. Classifying a borrower account as fraud follows the lender's board-approved process, including the borrower's right to be heard, and fraud reports to the regulator and suspicious transaction reports to FIU-IND stay with the responsible officers.
Portfolio reviews with SIP and goal check-insReview and growThe adviser reviews every pack, gives all recommendations and records the rationale, and risk profile updates are confirmed with the client. Automated messages never recommend schemes, promise returns or present past performance.
Top-up and renewal journeys approved by creditReview and growThe credit team approves the review criteria, every offer list and every final decision. Offers are never presented as pre-approved unless credit has approved them, and no limit is increased without the borrower's explicit, recorded consent.
